title: The Great Feminization Comes to Cornell
author: Helen Andrews
content:
![The Great Feminization Comes to
Cornell](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/10/AP26275638379582.jpg)

New York Governor Kathy Hochul emphasized her gender when asked on October 3
about her appointment of a special prosecutor to investigate a possible rape
at a fraternity house at Cornell University in 2024. Hochul is the first woman
to serve as New York's governor. Letitia James, the woman she appointed as
special prosecutor, is the state's first female attorney general. Seeing these
two women take on the Cornell case has a special symbolism, Hochul explained.
"I've heard from a lot of people," she said. "The image gives them comfort to
know that two women perhaps are looking at this differently than men would in
the same position."

She is right. The approach to the law reflected in the New York Democratic
officials' handling of the Cornell case represents a distinctively female
perspective. Unfortunately, that perspective is incompatible with the rule of
law.
